disposition_mapping.rationale: The council converged (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, and a conceding agentic_architect/maximalist) that assumption issuance stays FP&A-manager-owned and human-authored, especially the downside scenario (KB-04), while accepting agent-assisted drafting and versioning as a genuine improvement. The disposition is restructured rather than retained because versioning, a materiality re-issue trigger, and documented FX/stress methodology are added, but the function and its named accountable actor are unchanged.

Five of seven council members (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) held firmly against maximalist's proposal to merge this into assumption-issuance with CEO/CFO reduced to an override gate, on the grounds that an override gate inverts accountability for a strategic, credibility-bearing commitment with no reproducible evidence trail (KB-04 logic by extension). This synthesis adopts that majority reading of the unconstrained_by_design flag: latitude applies to mechanics, not to whether a human originates the judgment. Finance_domain's calibration-against-rolling-actuals enhancement is adopted as the one substantive change.

Unanimous rejection of maximalist's merger proposal (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect all held separately-owned). ABB-R-02 requires survival, and the council's shared 'augmented, not replaced' principle (hitl_designer/agentic_architect) is adopted: an advisory validation agent speeds drafting without taking write authority from the BU head.

Same reasoning as ABB-03: ABB-R-03 requires survival with a distinct owner, and the council rejected merging cost-centre budgeting with revenue planning or capex on accountability and data-provenance grounds (finance_domain, emerging_economy). Augmentation with an advisory agent is adopted; the step boundary and actor are unchanged.

Retained as its own step per the council's near-unanimous rejection of folding capex into a shared workspace (pragmatist's point that this would bury ABB-R-04 inside a larger submission). Finance_domain's and agentic_architect's capital-allocation-triage addition is adopted as the substantive enhancement, with emerging_economy's condition that FX/political-risk-sensitive items be routed to a human reviewer attached explicitly. The business-case-above-threshold input (ABB-R-04) is preserved unchanged.

The council agreed this step is the strongest legitimate automation target (agentic_architect, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, finance_domain) because consolidation, policy application and FX translation are mechanical and standard-governed (KB-06, KB-07), but it decisively rejected maximalist's dissolution of a discrete checkpoint into continuous ambient reconciliation: pragmatist, accounting_standards, hitl_designer and agentic_architect all held that KB-02's evidential-trail logic requires a nameable, timestamped, attestable sign-off, not just a log of clean runs. This synthesis adopts automated computation with a mandatory discrete attestation gate, finance_domain's completeness/data-quality gate, and emerging_economy's/accounting_standards' requirement that FX and policy logic remain locally inspectable rather than a head-office black box. Accounting_standards' intercompany-elimination-by-analogy is folded in as a recommendation given multi-entity structures.

The council's strongest and most consistent rejection was of maximalist's absorption of review-and-challenge into continuous exception-flagging inside consolidation (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards all held independently). Review and challenge is adversarial negotiation over defensible numbers, not error detection, and collapsing it removes the discrete round-trip where a submitter can contest an agent's characterization. This synthesis retains it as a distinct step, adopting the council's agreed enhancements: bounded/capped iterations with CFO escalation, mandatory gap analysis and downside-scenario stress-testing (finance_domain), and an advisory variance-insight agent (agentic_architect) that surfaces but does not conduct the negotiation.

Universal agreement across all seven council members: board approval is categorically a human governance act, protected by ABB-R-11, and must remain discrete and unmerged. The only addition, also unanimous, is making the full evidentiary package and any approval conditions explicit outputs.

The council converged, after direct back-and-forth, on a design combining agentic_architect's structural trigger constraint (the load agent cannot fire without a verified hash/version match to the board-approved artifact) with hitl_designer's and pragmatist's insistence on an affirmative, logged human attestation even on a successful match (not merely exception-based escalation), which maximalist and agentic_architect both explicitly conceded to in round 2. Emerging_economy's requirement for offline/batch-tolerant loading and accounting_standards'/finance_domain's governed post-lock amendment path (KB-05, applied forward) are folded in as non-negotiable features. Ordering (ABB-R-08) is preserved structurally as the trigger condition itself, not merely as process sequencing.

steps.description: An assumptions-drafting agent (read-only macro data connectors, a disclosed-methodology scenario generator) produces a draft calendar, central planning assumptions, central FX assumptions and a downside macro scenario. The FP&A manager remains the accountable author: every agent-proposed parameter and every override is logged with a diff, and the manager, not the agent, issues the final version-controlled assumption pack. The downside scenario's stress methodology must be chosen and owned by the FP&A manager (documented-model basis), not generated and merely spot-checked on exception. A materiality-triggered re-issue path exists if macro inputs move before submissions close. The FX rate-selection methodology (source, hierarchy, timing, treatment of multiple/parallel-rate regimes) is documented as part of the assumption pack so it is inspectable by local FP&A staff downstream at consolidation. If a data feed is stale or a scenario run fails validation, the agent halts and routes to the FP&A manager; a manual/offline assumption-setting path remains first-class, not a degraded fallback.
steps.name: Issue calendar and central planning assumptions (agent-assisted, human-curated)
outputs: Central FX assumptions (with documented rate methodology)
Downside macro scenario (with documented stress methodology)

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets, now explicitly calibrated against the latest actuals/rolling-forecast run-rate alongside the strategic plan, so targets are not purely aspirational. A target-simulation agent may run what-if scenarios as a decision-support tool, but it has no write authority: the executive originates the committed number, rather than reviewing and vetoing an agent-proposed one. This preserves the accountability trail for a resourcing/credibility commitment the board and every downstream submitter rely on.
steps.name: Set top-down targets (calibrated, executive-originated)

steps.description: Business unit heads continue to prepare and own revenue and volume plans, incorporating commercial judgment (pipeline, pricing, channel mix) that cannot be centralised without losing accountability. An intake-validation agent checks submissions against assumptions, prior actuals and internal consistency and flags anomalies, but never writes to the plan; the BU head's signed submission is what feeds consolidation. Tooling must remain usable offline/in spreadsheet-equivalent form where cloud planning tools are not available.
steps.name: Revenue and volume plans (augmented, locally owned)

steps.description: Cost centre owners continue to prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets. A validation agent checks headcount math, cost-per-FTE consistency and policy conformance and flags exceptions back to the owner, who remains the accountable submitter and may deviate from any template. The step tolerates manual/parallel HR record-keeping rather than assuming a clean HRIS feed.
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets (augmented, locally owned)

steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests and author the business case for requests above threshold; this judgment content remains human-authored, with agent assistance limited to ROI/NPV calculation as a tool invoked by the author. A capital-allocation triage (ranking aggregate demand against available capital, IRR/NPV and strategic-fit review) is added within this step so consolidation is never handed an unfunded capex plan. Any scoring/ranking tool used in triage must remain inspectable, and any request with material FX or political-risk exposure must be routed to a human reviewer rather than resolved by templated scoring.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests and capital allocation triage

steps.description: Submissions are consolidated into a draft three-statement budget on the same accounting basis as actuals. A consolidation engine automates aggregation, applies the accounting policies used for actuals, translates at the central FX assumptions using the documented rate methodology, and performs the three-statement tie-out, logging every policy application, rate used and submission version consumed. An explicit completeness/data-quality gate checks that no submission has been silently treated as zero or omitted. The engine halts and routes any reconciliation break, policy exception or incomplete submission to a named FP&A analyst, who is the accountable reviewer. Critically, the step produces a discrete, timestamped 'ready for review' artifact with an affirmative analyst sign-off certifying faithfulness and basis-consistency with actuals before it proceeds — continuous recomputation on every input change is acceptable, but a nameable, attestable checkpoint is mandatory and is not replaced by a log of clean runs. Where the budget spans a group structure, intercompany positions are identified and eliminated following the methodology used for actuals. FX and policy logic must remain inspectable by local FP&A staff, not a vendor black box usable only by a head-office super-user, and at least one trained backup must exist for this function given talent-concentration risk.
steps.name: Automated consolidation, completeness gate and analyst attestation
outputs: Draft three-statement budget (reconciled, logged and attested)

steps.description: The draft budget is reviewed and challenged with submitters through a bounded number of iteration rounds (capped in the calendar) rather than an open-ended cycle, with a CFO escalation rule if convergence is not reached. The step includes an explicit top-down-vs-bottom-up gap analysis against TS-02's targets and mandatory stress-testing of the consolidated plan against the downside macro scenario from TS-01, so the scenario is actually used rather than filed and forgotten. A variance-insight agent pre-computes driver bridges and flags material unexplained movements to focus the conversation, but the actual challenge, negotiation and revision remain a genuine adversarial human process between FP&A manager/CFO and submitters, with real authority to send submissions back; it is not compressed into an automated approval threshold or an embedded sign-off with no visible alternative framing. No accounting policy or FX basis fixed upstream may be altered invisibly during this process — any such change must be surfaced as a disclosed policy change.
inputs: Draft three-statement budget (reconciled, logged and attested)
steps.name: Review and challenge iterations (bounded, analytics-supported)
outputs: Gap analysis and downside-scenario stress-test results

steps.description: The board approves the budget, receiving the full evidentiary package: base and downside scenarios, the reconciled three statements, capex business cases above threshold, and a summary of what changed through challenge. Approval remains an irreducibly human, minuted decision, kept separate from the system mechanics of loading the budget. Any conditions attached to approval ('approved subject to X') are explicitly recorded as part of the output so they can be reconciled before lock.
inputs: Full decision package (scenarios, reconciliations, capex cases, challenge summary)
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: A load-and-lock agent is architecturally incapable of firing without a verified board-approval artifact as its trigger: it performs a hash/version match between the artifact about to be loaded and the one the board actually approved, and reconciles any board conditions. Even on a successful automated match, a named FP&A analyst must give an affirmative, logged attestation that the loaded version matches what the board approved before the lock commits — detection of a correct match and human confirmation of that detection are treated as two distinct evidentiary layers, not substitutes. The lock establishes the single authoritative baseline for variance analysis and archives the assumption set and capex business cases used. The mechanism tolerates batch/offline loading for entities without continuous connectivity. Once locked, the version is not silently edited: any post-lock correction of a material error must go through a governed amendment/re-forecast process, mirroring the error-correction discipline applied forward.
steps.name: Verified load, human attestation and lock
outputs: Archived assumption set and capex business cases
